article.headline: Winter storm advisory snarls central Illinois Thanksgiving travel with icy road conditions
article.summary: The National Weather Service issued a winter weather advisory for Springfield starting Wednesday afternoon through Thursday evening as snow threatens local commutes.
article.body:
Accumulations of 1 to 3 inches are expected from Canton to Petersburg and Springfield as a quick-hitting system moves into central Illinois. While higher snowfall amounts reaching 3 to 6 inches are possible in the Jacksonville area and counties to the west, most snow will accumulate on grassy and elevated surfaces, according to the National Weather Service. 

Travelers should prepare for slippery conditions that could impact Wednesday evening and Thursday morning commutes. Heavier snow bands remain a concern, as they may overcome warmer pavement and disrupt travel plans for those navigating the region during the Thanksgiving holiday. 

Drivers are advised to slow down and maintain extra distance between vehicles. Forecast models have recently downgraded earlier snowfall projections for the Springfield area, though uncertainties persist regarding the potential for a rain and snow mixture. 

Conditions are expected to transition as the system moves through, with the chance of precipitation remaining high at 90% to 100% through Thanksgiving Day. The forecast calls for a high near 39 degrees on Wednesday with north-northeast gusts reaching up to 24 mph by Thursday, before partly sunny skies return on Friday with highs near 43 degrees.

article.headline: Bills and Chiefs Clash for AFC Top Seed in Thanksgiving Week Showdown
article.summary: The Bills and Chiefs prepare for a pivotal Thanksgiving game as all 32 NFL teams remain in the playoff hunt heading into Week 12.
article.body:
With Thanksgiving approaching, every single one of the league's 32 teams remains mathematically eligible for a postseason berth. While the Arizona Cardinals face a remote possibility of elimination this week, they would require five specific outcomes, including a tie in the Packers-Rams game, to be knocked out. The upcoming schedule features 109 regular-season games remaining, with analysts simulating the final field to determine the eight division winners and the 14 total playoff participants.

Week 12 is defined by the high-stakes matchup between the 9-1 Buffalo Bills and 8-2 Kansas City Chiefs. According to NBC Sports, the victor of this Thanksgiving night game secures the inside track for the AFC's top seed and the accompanying first-round bye. The race tightened following recent losses by the Bengals and Jaguars, creating a crowded field at the top of the conference hierarchy.

In the AFC, the Denver Broncos hold an 8-2 record, maintaining a tiebreaker advantage over Kansas City based on common game results, while the Bengals and Jaguars both sit at 7-3. CBS Sports notes that Pittsburgh's decision to bench quarterback Aaron Rodgers following an ugly loss in Philadelphia marks the most significant personnel shift of the week. Despite the team's internal volatility, projections continue to keep the 6-4 Steelers in the postseason hunt.

The NFC playoff picture is similarly dense, with the 9-1 49ers leading the conference. The Thanksgiving schedule further intensifies the race, highlighted by a divisional battle between the 8-2 Lions and 8-2 Bears. Meanwhile, the 6-3-1 Giants have emerged as division leaders, and the 6-4 Packers and Rams are set to face off in a critical midweek encounter that will shape the conference standings.

Refereeing decisions throughout the game remained a significant point of contention, with Pochettino describing the initial booking of Tielemans as difficult to understand.

Manchester United will now look to regroup as they prepare for their upcoming fixture against Brentford. This weekend's match marks the first time Pochettino will lead the team at Old Trafford, where he faces the challenge of turning around a campaign that has seen only four victories thus far.

article.headline: Singapore Identity Cards Feature Full NRIC Numbers on Address Stickers From December
article.summary: Starting December 1, the Immigration and Checkpoints Authority will issue address stickers displaying full NRIC numbers for new residential address updates.
article.body: Partial NRIC numbers are being phased out by the Singapore Government because they lack the reliability required for accurate individual identification. The Immigration and Checkpoints Authority (ICA) noted that some citizens share the same name or partial identification numbers, prompting this shift toward full numbers to ensure the sticker correctly corresponds to the identity card holder. For residents, this change means that any address sticker issued or replaced on or after December 1 will feature the complete NRIC, allowing for a direct and verified match against the identity card itself. Current stickers featuring only partial numbers remain valid and do not require replacement. This update is part of a broader government transition away from using partial identifiers across the public sector to improve security and precision. Residents who have previously applied to change their address or requested a replacement sticker will follow the established process: receiving a PIN by mail, verifying it on the ICA website, and subsequently applying the new sticker to the back of their physical card. Under the National Registration Act, all identity card holders are required to report a change of residence within 28 days of moving. Failure to report a change of address can result in severe penalties, including a fine of up to $5,000, imprisonment of up to five years, or both. The ICA manages these updates through its online change of address e-service, which remains the primary portal for residents to maintain their current residential records with the authorities.

The footage shows the pair approaching a massive staircase leading toward Doom’s throne, marking the first time these characters have faced the actor since his original turn as Iron Man in the 2019 film. Reports from MovieWeb note that this trio last shared the screen seven years ago during the final confrontation with Thanos.

As the studio enters the final stages of marketing for its fifth Avengers movie, the film is set for a wide release on December 18. While specific plot details remain under wraps, the narrative will integrate legacy actors who have portrayed these roles for over two decades. article.body:
After flying high as Superman, David Corenswet trades his cape for a jersey to portray the unlikely journey of John Tuggle, the final player selected in the 1983 NFL draft by the New York Giants. The film showcases Tuggle's defiance of expectations both on the gridiron and in his personal life, a performance that is already generating significant buzz as potential Oscar-worthy work ahead of its release. Corenswet stars alongside Michael Shannon, who plays Giants coach Bill Parcells, and Isabel May, who portrays Tuggle's love interest, Katie. 

For football fans and cinema-goers, this true story offers an intimate look at the dedication required to defy the label of an underdog. The production highlights the intense bond between a player and a head coach, capturing the moment the New York Giants picked Tuggle in the final round—a decision that forever altered the trajectory of his professional career. According to Yahoo, the film explores how remarkable perseverance can overcome even the most daunting challenges in the sports world.

Directed by Jonathan Levine with a script by Nick Santora, the film features an ensemble cast including David Krumholtz, Tuwaine Barrett, Thaddeus LaGrone, Alexander England, Spencer House, and Tandi Wright. Produced by a large team including David Ellison and Dana Goldberg, the project has already begun promotional activities. 

Fans looking for an early look can participate in ticket giveaways through Audacy, which is offering seats for an advanced screening. This special showing is scheduled to take place at the Cinemark Egyptian Theater in Arundel Mills Mall on December 16, 2026, at 7pm. Following these promotional screenings, the full theatrical release is slated for December 25, 2026.

article.headline: Celtic eyes crucial Europa League points against Torreense in Portuguese league showdown
article.summary: Celtic faces Torreense in the Europa League on Thursday, November 26, 2026, at 8pm in Leiria.
article.body:
Celtic arrives at the Dr. Magalhães Pessoa Stadium facing a unique European challenge, as they prepare to play a team not currently competing in their country’s top domestic flight. Torreense, a second-division side, secured their place in this competition after a historic cup run that saw them defeat Sporting Lisbon to claim the first major trophy in their 109-year existence. The match is set to take place 60 miles away from the home ground of the Portuguese club because their own facility, with a 2,500-seat capacity, failed to meet mandatory UEFA requirements.

This fixture represents a critical juncture for Celtic as they attempt to mount a comeback in the competition. Currently sitting 32nd in the 36-team league phase, the club is striving to become the first side to reach the knockout stages after losing their opening three matches. Securing points here is vital for manager Martin O’Neill, who must also balance the squad’s workload against upcoming domestic commitments, including a weekend showdown at Tynecastle against Hearts and a clash against Dundee next Wednesday.

Manager Martin O’Neill has confirmed that Kasper Hogh and Haissem Hassan will participate in the match. Meanwhile, the club has bolstered its options by adding Jota to the Europa League squad in place of the injured Mika Baur. While Auston Trusty is expected to return to the fold following his international duty, Jota’s involvement remains a point of interest after his recent recovery from a long-term knee injury. Torreense enters the encounter in 19th position, aiming to build on their six points from the opening four games. The match will be broadcast on TNT Sports 3, with coverage beginning at 7:45pm ahead of the 8pm kick-off.

article.headline: India snatches toss and debuts Gurnoor Brar in second test showdown
article.summary: India captain Shubman Gill chose to bowl at Hagley Oval on Friday as his team looks to break the deadlock in the second test against New Zealand.
article.body:
Gurnoor Brar makes his debut for India in Christchurch, stepping in for Prasidh Krishna to bolster the pace attack. The decision follows a heavy workload for the bowlers in the first test at the Basin Reserve, a match where India controlled long periods of play before it ended in a draw. Both teams enter the contest with the series locked at 0-0, desperate for a result to bolster their standings in the World Test Championship.

This match carries significant stakes for both squads as they fight to climb the World Test Championship table. New Zealand currently holds third place, while India sits in fourth. Securing a victory at Hagley Oval is essential for either side to improve their chances of reaching the final. India’s captain Shubman Gill noted that his pace bowlers are fresh and ready for the challenge, while New Zealand captain Tom Latham opted for an unchanged lineup despite his personal struggles in the series opener.

Conditions at Hagley Oval may favor the bowlers early on. According to reports from the venue, the pitch features a green covering with grass, though it is expected to be moist and slower on the first day. Latham noted that while he also intended to bowl, he expects the surface to quicken as the match progresses into the second and third days. Following the persistent rain in Christchurch that lasted until early Thursday afternoon, the state of the surface remains a primary focus for both team strategies.

India will field a side including Jaiswal, Rahul, Padikkal, Gill, Pant, Jurel, Sundar, Kamboj, Akash Deep, Bumrah, and the debutant Brar. New Zealand remains unchanged with Latham, Conway, Nicholls, Ravindra, Mitchell, Blundell, Phillips, Smith, Jamieson, Henry, and Duffy.

While some brands are slashing their most iconic bestsellers to half price, others are focusing on volume, with Mr Porter currently offering over 14,000 products at reduced rates. According to British GQ, the Wax checked overshirts famously worn by Bradley Cooper are among the items now available at 50% off. Meanwhile, Uniqlo is applying discounts to its higher-end subdivisions, including its collaborative collections with JW Anderson and its Uniqlo U line. For shoppers, these sales serve as a timely opportunity to secure wardrobe staples like heavy winter coats and dress shirts at a significant markup reduction.

For those not focused on apparel, the Black Friday market extends into everyday necessities and luxury skincare. The Guardian reports that Pukka Herbs herbal tea Advent calendars have dropped in price to £7.30, down from £13.35, while sustainable deodorant brand Fussy is offering a 25% site-wide discount using the code BLACK. These deals are specifically targeted at consumers balancing gift-buying urgency with the desire to stock up on household essentials, such as laundry detergent and SPF skincare products, which are also seeing deep price cuts.

The breadth of the current sales cycle suggests a strategic push by retailers to capture consumer spending before the holiday season hits its peak. Experts note that the urgency is driven by the proximity to payday and the desire to clear inventory across both mundane essentials and luxury grails. Whether shopping for high-performance sunscreen or sustainable toiletries, current market activity indicates that consumers are finding record-low prices on tested goods that were previously sold at higher margins. article.headline: Yaté and Thio face orange weather alert as heavy rains hit territory
article.summary: Météo-France has placed Yaté and Thio under orange alert for heavy rain and storms until Friday afternoon.
article.body:
Up to 150 mm of rain may fall locally in just twelve hours between Thursday night and Friday in Yaté and Thio, according to Météo-France. While these two communes face an orange alert, the rest of New Caledonia remains under a yellow weather watch. In these yellow-alert areas, meteorologists forecast accumulation totals of 50 to 100 mm over a twelve-hour period.

Following heavy rainfall, authorities urge the public to limit travel to essential needs only. Residents are advised not to cross flooded roads or bridges, even on foot, and to keep children away from streams and rivers. The municipality of Ouégoa warned that rising waters could potentially submerge the Mission bridge at Bondé, noting that the radier at the Paimboa tribe has already been inundated.

According to NoumeaPost, a slow meteorological improvement is expected starting Friday, particularly in the South, where showers are becoming less frequent. However, the Northeast remains exposed to stormy downpours capable of generating significant local accumulation. Winds are generally blowing from the East between 15 and 20 knots, with the possibility of gusts during thunderstorms.

Looking ahead to the weekend, conditions will remain very cloudy across the country. Saturday will bring frequent and locally sustained showers, especially on the East Coast, the mountain range, Belep, the Isle of Pines, Lifou, and Maré. By Sunday, although the weather will stay cloudy, precipitation is expected to become more infrequent. Temperatures are forecast to rise, climbing above seasonal averages by the end of the weekend as the wind shifts and eases across the region.

news.title: Varias demandas alegan que el ICE maltrató a ciudadanos estadounidenses y a reclusos en un centro de detención con fines de lucro
news.og_title: Varias demandas alegan que el ICE maltrató a ciudadanos estadounidenses y a reclusos en un centro de detención con fines de lucro
news.og_desc:
En Estados Unidos, dos personas que fueron arrestadas de forma brutal por agentes federales durante las amplias redadas migratorias de 2025 en el área metropolitana de la ciudad de Chicago han presentado demandas separadas contra el Gobierno de Trump.  Dayanne Figueroa y Luis Jesús Acosta Gutiérrez formaron parte de las personas detenidas cuando cientos de agentes federales llegaron al estado de Illinois para llevar a cabo la campaña represiva contra la inmigración conocida como Operación Midway Blitz. Agentes federales arrestaron a Gutiérrez tras enfrentarse durante horas contra miembros de la comunidad y vecinos que se habían congregado para tratar de protegerlo, a quienes les lanzaron gas lacrimógeno y gas pimienta.  Figueroa, quien es madre soltera y ciudadana estadounidense, acababa de dejar a su hija de cinco años en la escuela cuando agentes del Servicio de Inmigración de Estados Unidos (ICE, por sus siglas en inglés) embistieron su vehículo, la bajaron de este jalándola de las piernas, la arrojaron al pavimento y la inmovilizaron boca abajo con las rodillas. Según la demanda, uno de los agentes colocó una rodilla cerca de una incisión de una cirugía renal reciente, lo que le provocó a Figueroa un dolor insoportable. Figueroa fue arrestada sin una orden judicial, a pesar de haber dicho repetidas veces a los agentes que era ciudadana estadounidense. 
En noticias relacionadas, la familia de un ciudadano estadounidense de la ciudad de Pharr, estado de Texas, está considerando iniciar acciones legales contra el Gobierno de Trump después de que imágenes de cámaras corporales mostraran a agentes federales enmascarados deteniendo a Domingo Vásquez en una obra de construcción situada en la ciudad texana de Álamo. La madre de Vásquez afirma que este padece una discapacidad intelectual y que, en el momento de su arresto, no portaba su identificación. Vásquez había estado trabajando en la obra de construcción con su tío. 
Mientras tanto, cuatro inmigrantes, incluidos dos hombres transgénero, que estuvieron detenidos en una cárcel con fines de lucro del ICE en la localidad de Basile, estado de Luisiana, afirman haber sido víctimas de violaciones, agresiones sexuales, mensajes de odio contra la comunidad LGBTQ y trabajos forzosos por parte de miembros del personal penitenciario. Los cuatro inmigrantes han presentado una demanda contra la compañía penitenciaria privada Geo Group y dos exempleados del Centro de Procesamiento de Inmigrantes del Sur de Luisiana, incluido el exdirector adjunto de la prisión. Los demandantes afirman que también se les negó atención médica y que fueron recluidos en régimen de aislamiento en represalia por denunciar los abusos que allí sufrían.
